title: Chord Progressions
description: Play the four-chord loop behind countless pop songs, I-V-vi-IV, and meet its older cousin, I-vi-IV-V.

steps.title: Chords get numbers
steps.description:
A chord progression is just a series of chords played in order. Musicians number the chords in a key with Roman numerals: uppercase for major, lowercase for minor. In C major:

• I = C
• ii = Dm
• iii = Em
• IV = F
• V = G
• vi = Am
• vii° = Bdim

Plenty of pop songs get by on just three or four of these.

steps.title: The four-chord song
steps.description: I-V-vi-IV (C, G, Am, F) is everywhere in pop. 'Let It Be', 'No Woman, No Cry' and 'With or Without You' all use it (each in its own key), along with hundreds of others. Play it through and you'll probably recognize it.

steps.title: Start on C (I)
steps.description: Begin with C major, the home chord.
steps.hint: C, E, G. Thumb, middle finger, pinky.

steps.title: Up to G (V)
steps.description: Move to G major. It's chord V, and it pushes the music forward.
steps.hint: G, B, D. Any octave or order works.

steps.title: Down to Am (vi)
steps.description: Now A minor. This is where the progression gets its touch of sadness.
steps.hint: A, C, E. All white keys.

steps.title: Over to F (IV)
steps.description: Finish with F major. From here the loop wants to head straight back to C, so try playing all four a few times in a row.
steps.hint: F, A, C. Coming from A minor, you can keep A and C and just move E up to F.

steps.title: The '50s progression
steps.description: Shuffle the same chords into I-vi-IV-V (C, Am, F, G) and you get the sound of 1950s and early '60s doo-wop and pop, like 'Earth Angel' and 'Stand By Me'. Same four chords, but putting the minor one second gives it a gentler, more nostalgic feel.

steps.title: Which one is vi?
steps.description: In the key of C, which chord is vi?
